rationale:
bugs_open/201: three discovery checks name page-content-writer as their HandlerAgent and dispatch it DIRECTLY. Every such dispatch hard-fails before writing anything. 11 of 11 attempts on 2026-08-04, all with the same error: 'page-content-writer planned its own sections and none are ready — no page can be written.'

THE MECHANISM, and it is not what the error text suggests. bugs_closed/087 gave page-content-writer a self-plan fallback for callers that supply no section_plan (migration 309). That fallback plans from `input_data.current_page.sections`. A discovery check's spec has NO `sections` key at all — measured, not assumed: all 14 page-content-writer work items that have ever existed fleet-wide carry exactly {check, findings, fix, original_pipeline, page_id, page_name, page_url} (literal_markdown) or {check, findings, original_pipeline, page_id, page_name, patterns} (placeholder_contact). `spec ? 'sections'` is FALSE on every one. So plan_sections takes its EMPTY-INPUT early return — `ready_count: 0, reason: "no sections to plan"` (plan_sections_action.go:867-875) — and the run dies at fail_no_ready_sections. The failure is 'no sections were supplied', not 'the sections were not ready'; the error message describes the symptom and hides the cause, which is why this reads as a data problem and is actually a routing problem.

WHY page-build-handler IS THE ANSWER, and why this is completing a migration rather than inventing one. page-build-handler does not trust the caller for its section list: load_spec_sections (action load_page_sections_from_spec) reads site_specs.site_plan — authoritative — with a pages.sections fallback, and only then runs plan_sections. So it is structurally immune to the spec shape that breaks the direct route. It is also PROVEN on already-built pages, which is the case 201 flagged as unverified: content_rewrite 19 complete and empty_section 12 complete on pages that already have page_components rows (measured 2026-08-05), against page-content-writer's 14 items with ZERO genuine successes (12 failed, 1 'complete' that provably wrote nothing per 201 Symptom 2, 1 triaged). And check_empty_sections.go ALREADY made exactly this migration — its header records 'HandlerAgent: page-build-handler (was page-content-writer)' — as did save_sections_claims_guard.go. These three checks are the un-migrated tail, not a new direction.

ONE OF THE THREE IS A STRAIGHTFORWARD INCONSISTENCY, independent of the argument above. check_component_standards' empty-page-sections sub-check files ItemType 'needs_content_page' — the SAME item type write_build_items produces — and write_build_items routes that type to page-build-handler (load_work_item_actions.go:242-243). One item type was being routed to two different handlers depending on which producer filed it.

THE GENERAL RULE WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN, in check_sectionless_pages.go's own header: 'HandlerAgent is page-build-handler (NOT page-content-writer): the build handler is the workflow that runs load_spec_sections -> plan_sections, which is where the sibling fallback lives. Routing straight to the writer would bypass it.' page-content-writer is not removed from the estate and is not deprecated — page-build-handler SPAWNS it (spawn_content_writer -> call_content_writer) after planning. This change stops it being called without the wrapper that makes it work.

WHAT I AM DELIBERATELY NOT DOING, and I want this on the record because it is the tempting next edit and it is dangerous. After this change NO producer anywhere files a work item with handler_agent='page-content-writer' (grep across platform/ internal/ pkg/ returns zero). site-work-orchestrator's build_items_loop is gated by load_work_items with handler_agent='page-content-writer', so that loop becomes permanently unfeedable. I am NOT 'fixing' that by repointing its filter at page-build-handler: build-dispatch-loop already consumes those items, so a second consumer of the same rows invites double-dispatch, and this estate has a filed history of exactly that class. The loop was already unreachable in practice — it has never run (absent from agent_run_stats, which has no reaper), and its only possible inputs were the items that hard-fail. This change makes an existing deadness explicit rather than creating it. It is recorded in bugs_open/201 and in the 194 lane, whose acceptance check depended on that loop and is now known to be blocked behind this bug rather than behind a site choice.

SCOPE. Symptom 2 (the item that reached 'complete' having written nothing, and mark_complete trusting handler_result blindly) is NOT addressed here. 201's own §2 says explicitly not to fix it before this one, because a test against the current broken routing would look like it 'worked' by reaching complete while still writing nothing. This is fix-1 of two.
submitter: bugfix_201 lane (re-route three discovery checks off direct page-content-writer dispatch, 2026-08-05)

plan.summary: Three discovery checks route work items at page-content-writer and dispatch it directly. The writer self-plans from `current_page.sections`, which a discovery spec never carries, so plan_sections returns ready_count:0 ('no sections to plan') and every dispatch hard-fails before writing — 11 of 11. Re-point all three at page-build-handler, which sources its section list from site_specs.site_plan instead of from the caller's spec, is proven on already-built pages, and already spawns page-content-writer behind its own planning step. Completes the migration check_empty_sections.go and save_sections_claims_guard.go already made.

grounded_in: THE CAUSE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED (clients_db, 2026-08-05): SELECT wi.item_type, (wi.spec ? 'sections') AS has_sections, string_agg of jsonb_object_keys, count(*) FROM site_work_items wi WHERE wi.handler_agent='page-content-writer' GROUP BY 1,2,3 => literal_markdown | false | {check,findings,fix,original_pipeline,page_id,page_name,page_url} | 12 ;; placeholder_contact | false | {check,findings,original_pipeline,page_id,page_name,patterns} | 2. has_sections is FALSE on all 14 rows that have ever existed.

THE EARLY RETURN THAT FIRES, plan_sections_action.go:867-875: 'if len(sectionNames) == 0 { return map[string]interface{}{ "sections_ready": []interface{}{}, ..., "ready_count": 0, "reason": "no sections to plan" }, nil }'. sectionNames comes from inputs.GetRaw("sections").

THE TWO SECTION SOURCES, side by side, from live agent_definitions 2026-08-05. page-content-writer.plan_sections.config.sections = 'input_data.current_page.sections' (the CALLER's blob). page-build-handler.plan_sections.config.sections = 'spec_sections.sections', where spec_sections is the output_field of load_spec_sections, action 'load_page_sections_from_spec', described in its own config as 'Load sections from site_specs.site_plan (authoritative), fall back to pages.sections'.

page-build-handler IS PROVEN ON ALREADY-BUILT PAGES — the exact question bugs_open/201 §1 asked and could not answer. SELECT wi.item_type, wi.status, EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM page_components pc WHERE pc.page_id=wi.page_id) AS page_already_built, count(*) FROM site_work_items wi WHERE wi.handler_agent='page-build-handler' AND wi.page_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2,3 => content_rewrite|complete|true|19 ;; empty_section|complete|true|12 ;; empty_internal_href|complete|true|1. So it does not hit the 'no ready sections' wall on a built page.

THE COMPARISON THAT MAKES THAT NUMBER MEAN SOMETHING: page-content-writer, same table, all history — 12 failed, 1 complete, 1 triaged. The single 'complete' is bugs_open/201 Symptom 2, proven at artefact level by its filer to have written nothing. Zero genuine successes against page-build-handler's 32.

THIS MIGRATION HAS ALREADY BEEN MADE TWICE, and this is the tail: check_empty_sections.go header line 7 'HandlerAgent: "page-build-handler" (was "page-content-writer")'; save_sections_claims_guard.go:23 carries the same note. empty_section's 12 completes above are that migration working.

THE RULE STATED IN OUR OWN SOURCE, check_sectionless_pages.go header (quoted in bugs_open/201 §1): 'HandlerAgent is page-build-handler (NOT page-content-writer): the build handler is the workflow that runs load_spec_sections -> plan_sections, which is where the sibling fallback lives. Routing straight to the writer would bypass it.'

THE INCONSISTENCY IN THE THIRD CHECK: write_build_items assigns handlerAgent := "page-build-handler" with itemType := "needs_content_page" (load_work_item_actions.go:242-243), and every entry in its availableBuilders map (:220-225: content, index, landing, blog-index, blog-post) resolves to page-build-handler. check_component_standards filed the same 'needs_content_page' type at page-content-writer.

GUARD PROVEN TO FAIL ON A BAD VALUE, not merely to pass on a good one: with HandlerAgent set to "bogus-nonexistent-handler", 'go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/' FAILS — TestEveryCheckHandlerAgentExistsOrIsADeclaredGap, handler_coverage_test.go:151, 'check in check_literal_markdown.go routes work at handler agent "bogus-nonexistent-handler", which is not a known agent and is not a declared gap.' Restored to page-build-handler, the package is ok. page-build-handler is already present in knownHandlerAgents, so the new value is inside the guard's vocabulary rather than exempt from it.
BUILD AND TEST AT THIS TREE: 'gofmt -l' clean on all four edited files; 'go build ./platform/...' succeeds; 'go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/' ok 0.06s.

THE CONSEQUENCE I AM DECLARING RATHER THAN HIDING: after this change 'grep -rn HandlerAgent: "page-content-writer" --include=*.go platform/ internal/ pkg/' returns ZERO rows. site-work-orchestrator's load_work_items filters handler_agent='page-content-writer' (its step config, live) so its build_items_loop can no longer be fed by anything. It was already unreachable in practice — site-work-orchestrator is ABSENT from agent_run_stats (which has no reaper and does track orchestrator-shaped agents), and its only possible inputs were the items that hard-fail. NOT repointing that filter at page-build-handler is deliberate: build-dispatch-loop already consumes those rows and a second consumer invites double-dispatch.

THE DEPENDENCY THIS UNBLOCKS: bugs_closed/194's live acceptance (check 3b) needs a dispatch that reaches save_page_sections inside site-work-orchestrator's build loop. The only work item fleet-wide that the loop could load is dad119c9-de2c-456d-9177-455a38df0ce4 (mortgagecalculator.co.uk, literal_markdown, triaged, attempt_count 1) — which bugs_open/201 §3 already predicts will fail identically on its remaining attempts, and whose site is LOCKED (sites.locked_at 2026-08-03 10:30Z, locked_by 'mortgagecalculator-adoption-lane: composition+design done; held pending owner decision on page rebuilds').

SCOPE LIMIT STATED BY THE BUG ITSELF, bugs_open/201 §2: 'do not fix this before fix-1, or a test against the current broken routing will look like it "worked" (reached complete) when it still didn't write anything.' Symptom 2 and mark_complete's blind trust of handler_result are therefore untouched here.
